gate2.variant_view: The market views Sony as an undifferentiated, struggling conglomerate where the volatility of the entertainment business is inextricably linked to the declining electronics hardware division. We believe that by spinning off a minority stake in the entertainment business, the market will re-rate these high-quality, high-margin assets at their true intrinsic value, removing them from the conglomerate discount. This separation will force management to instill greater financial discipline across the remaining electronics business [D03; D07].

final.memo:
Sony Corporation is a classic example of a company suffering from a significant conglomerate discount, where high-quality entertainment assets are hidden behind a struggling electronics business [D01; D03]. Despite the company's recent return to profitability, with ¥43 billion in net income for the year ended March 2013, the market continues to undervalue its disparate segments [D02; D03]. 

Our sum-of-the-parts analysis values Sony at approximately ¥2,650 per share, based on a 12x EBITDA multiple for the entertainment business and a recovery-adjusted value for the remaining operations [D03]. This compares favorably to our entry price of ¥1,855, representing a compelling risk/reward skew of roughly 40% upside against a hard valuation floor at 0.85x book value [D03; D04]. 

The market currently fails to differentiate between the volatility of the electronics hardware business and the underlying value of the Pictures and Music franchises [D05]. By forcing a partial IPO of up to 20% of the entertainment division, we believe we can eliminate the conglomerate discount and force the electronics segment to adopt the financial discipline displayed by its peers, such as Canon, which generates a 9.3% operating margin compared to Sony's 3.4% [D03; D06]. 

We are engaging with CEO Kazuo Hirai and the Board to demand this structural separation as a critical step toward accountability [D03]. Our role is that of a constructivist shareholder; should management remain unresponsive to this public plan, we are prepared to escalate our stake and increase pressure ahead of future annual meetings [D03; D07]. We view this as a primary, high-conviction position in our Japanese portfolio, sized at 8% of NAV to account for the significant potential for value unlock [D07].
